images.title: Three right angles leave 90° for the fourth
images.purpose: Shows that a quadrilateral with three right angles must have a fourth angle of 360° − 270° = 90°.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large rectangle in the centre with three corners marked and the fourth corner highlighted, and one sum under it.
images.exact_structure: One quadrilateral in dark outline, wider than tall, with all four corners at right angles. At the top left, top right and bottom right corners a small teal (#0072B2) square right angle mark, each labelled 90° in teal, three marks in all. At the bottom left corner a small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) square right angle mark labelled 90° in reddish purple. Under the shape, centred, the line 360° − 270° = 90°. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°, so three right angles force the fourth.
images.description: Shows that a quadrilateral with three right angles must have a fourth angle of 360° − 270° = 90°.

image_decisions.why: Three marked right angles and one highlighted fourth turn the angle sum into a visible reason.
